children: Intel Corp. (INTC, Financials), the semiconductor manufacturer, delivered stronger third-quarter results but issued a weaker fourth-quarter outlook as a factory shutdown, PC weakness and supply constraints weighed on expectations.
Third quarter sales was $16.5 billion, with non-GAAP EPS of $0.52 and gross margin of 44.1%.
Data Center and AI sales was $7.3 billion with operating profit of $3 billion, Intel's best sector revenue increase in 15 years.
But guidance for the fourth quarter underwhelmed. Intel predicts revenue of $15 billion to $16 billion, non-GAAP EPS of $0.25 and gross margin of 38 percent.
An accident at its Fab 28 plant in Israel would likely affect fourth-quarter sales by around $300 million and lower gross margin by about 200 basis points.
Intel also sees its client computing sales dropping by more than 20% quarter-over-quarter, as the PC correction intensifies.
Looking ahead, management sees healthy demand for server CPUs, forecasting the addressable market may grow from roughly $40 billion to more than $200 billion over a five-year period.
The next driver is recovery at Fab 28 and Intel's ability to turn increased server demand into better free cash flow.

title: Intel Slides as Weak Q4 Outlook Overshadows Data Center Growth
